europe_now.title: Mass Demonstrations and Security Response in France
europe_now.summary: Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators participated in widespread protests across France amid heightened security measures and warnings from the interior ministry. The demonstrations, marking a third consecutive weekend of unrest, saw clashes between police and protesters in Paris.

sources.headline: Some 320,000 demonstrators take part in largely peaceful protests across France
Thousands demonstrate in Paris as protests spread across Europe

europe_now.title: Constitutional Crisis and Power Struggle in Poland
europe_now.summary: A severe rule-of-law crisis unfolded in Poland as the country's president engaged in a physical confrontation with judges amidst an escalating power struggle at the constitutional court. The confrontations drew large crowds of protesters to gather outside the top court.

sources.headline: Protesters gather at Poland's Top court

top_stories.title: Humanitarian Evacuation from Occupied Ukraine
top_stories.summary: Ukrainian civilians who spent years trapped in Russian-occupied territory have successfully completed an evacuation operation and reunited with their families. Evacuees reported enduring severe hardships, including severe food shortages, during their time in the frontline city.

sources.headline: 'We came back from hell', say Ukrainians after years in Russia-occupied frontline city
Residents from Russian-occupied Oleshky reunite with families after evacuation operation

top_stories.title: German Protests and Cost of Living Unrest
top_stories.summary: Demonstrations addressing cost-of-living pressures and education funding turned violent in Germany, resulting in reported clashes with police and the looting of shops. The protests reflect growing civil unrest among younger demographics across the region.

sources.headline: Shops looted as German cost of living protests turn violent

top_stories.title: Diplomatic Tensions Over Russia's Global Stance
top_stories.summary: European officials have expressed strong opposition to any potential return of Vladimir Putin to the G20, warning that it risks normalizing war crimes. Meanwhile, ministers remain deeply divided over Russia's presence at international diplomatic forums.

sources.headline: Putin’s potential G20 comeback risks normalizing Russian war crimes, says Kallas
